title: Nuclear startup in Texas applies for connection to the power grid
source_used: Energy Connects, relaying a Bloomberg report (6 Oct 2026); Bloomberg is the reporter
key_facts: Blue Energy Global Inc., a Maryland-based nuclear startup, has applied to connect its project to the grid operated by the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT).
The grid operator says it is the first-ever application for small modular reactors (small nuclear reactors).
The company plans as many as five 300 MW nuclear systems, and as much as 1.5 GW of small reactors to supply a Crusoe Inc. data centre; the reported plan would power about 260,000 Texas homes.
The reactors use a 300 MW design from GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy; the company expects the first to go into service in 2033.
The project also plans about 1 GW of natural gas generation, with two units due to begin operating in 2030 and 2031, and the gas systems have their own application to connect.
Texas already has four large conventional reactors at South Texas Project and Comanche Peak, with more than 5 GW of capacity.
quote_evidence: Blue Energy Global Inc., a nuclear startup, has applied to connect to the Texas power grid, the first company to seek permission to deliver electricity from next-generation reactors in a push to meet surging demand from data centers.
The grid operator said it's the first-ever application for small modular reactors.
Blue Energy plans to build as many as five 300-megawatt nuclear systems.
why_it_matters_hint: First small-reactor application to the Texas grid, tied to data centre power demand; the reactors are not due until 2033.
